===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=direction|:inh|enm:doun<id:direction>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|doun}}, {{m|enm|doune||down}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dūne||down}}, [[w:Apheresis (linguistics)|aphetic]] form of {{m|ang|adūne||down, downward}}, from earlier {{m|ang|ofdūne|t=down|lit=off the hill}}, from {{m|ang|of||of, off of}} + {{m|ang|dūn||hill, mount, dune, down}}. More at Etymology 2 below. For the development from directional phrases to prepositions, compare {{ncog|ofs|dene|t=down|pos=adverb|lit=(to the) floor}}, {{ncog|gml|dāle|t=down, downwards|lit=(in/to the) dale/valley}}, whence {{ncog|nds-de|dal||down}}. Compare also {{ncog|stq|deel|t=down|lit=to/into the dale}}, {{ncog|fy|del||down}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|doon||down}}.

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|-,further}}

# {{lb|en|comparable}} From a higher position to a [[lower]] one; [[downwards]].
#: {{ux|en|The cat jumped '''down''' from the table.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=6|passage=She was so mad she wouldn't speak to me for quite a spell, but at last I coaxed her into going up to Miss Emmeline's room and fetching '''down''' a tintype of the missing Deacon man.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1967| author=w:Barbara Sleigh| title=w:Jessamy| edition=year_published| location=Sevenoaks, Kent| publisher=Bloomsbury| isbn=0 340 19547 9| page=48| passage=To her humiliation Jessamy found there were tears trickling '''down''' her cheeks.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year = 1967| author=w:Barbara Sleigh| title = w:Jessamy| year_published = 1993| location=Sevenoaks, Kent| publisher=Bloomsbury| isbn=0 340 19547 9| page = 122| passage = Through the open front door ran Jessamy, '''down''' the steps to where Kitto was sitting at the bottom with the pram beside him.}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}
# To or towards what is considered the bottom of something, irrespective of whether this is presently physically lower.
#: {{ux|en|Go '''down''' to the bottom of the page.}}
#: {{ux|en|As I lay on my back, a pain shot '''down''' from my neck to my waist.}}
# {{lb|en|comparable}} At a lower or further [[place]] or [[position]] along a set path.
#: {{ux|en|His place is farther '''down''' the road.}}
#: {{ux|en|The company was well '''down''' the path to bankruptcy.}}
#* {{RQ:Weyman Chippinge Borough|I|01|passage=It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking '''down''' Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street. He wore shepherd's plaid trousers and the swallow-tail coat of the day, with a figured muslin cravat wound about his wide-spread collar.}}
# To the [[south|south]] (as south is at the bottom of typical maps).
#: {{ux|en|I went '''down''' to Miami for a conference.}}
# Away from the city (regardless of direction).
#: {{ux|en|He went '''down''' to Cavan.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''down''' on the farm}}
#: {{ux|en|'''down''' to the country}}
#* '''1722''', {{w|Daniel Defoe}}, ''{{w|A Journal of the Plague Year}},'' London: E. Nutt ''et al.,'' p.{{nbsp}}12,<sup>[https://archive.org/details/b30518362/page/12/mode/1up]</sup>
#*: But then my Servant who I had intended to take '''down''' with me <nowiki>[</nowiki>''[[i.e.]]'' from London to [[Bedfordshire]]<nowiki>]</nowiki>, deceiv’d me;
# At or towards any place that is visualised as 'down' by virtue of local features or local convention, or arbitrarily, irrespective of direction or elevation change.
#: {{cot|en|over}}
#: {{ux|en|She lives '''down''' by the park.}}
# Forward, straight ahead.
#: {{ux|en|At the first intersection turn left and walk '''down''', then turn right.}}
# {{anchor|Adv_rail}}{{lb|en|rail transport}} In the direction leading away from the principal terminus, away from [[milepost]] zero.
# {{lb|en|UK|academia|dated}} Away from [[Oxford]] or [[Cambridge]].
#: {{ux|en|He's gone back '''down''' to Newcastle for Christmas.}}
# To a subordinate or less prestigious position or rank.
#: {{ux|en|Smith was sent '''down''' to the minors to work on his batting.}}
#: {{ux|en|After the incident, Kelly went '''down''' to Second Lieutenant.}}
# {{lb|en|sport}} Towards the opponent's side (in ball-sports).
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Daily Telegraph| title=Frustrated Prince Harry howls as he misses open goal| date=25 May 2015| url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/othersports/polo/11627962/Frustrated-Prince-Harry-howls-as-he-misses-open-goal.html| passage=The charity match, played Sunday afternoon at Cirencester Park Polo Club in Gloucestershire, reached a dramatic climax when Prince Harry tore '''down''' the pitch but failed to score what was described as an “open goal”.}}
#* {{quote-web|en| title=LBW explained| date=Sept 2005| url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/cricket/rules_and_equipment/6126324.stm| passage=By moving further down the pitch, the batsman lengthens the distance between the ball and the stumps.}}
# So as to lessen quantity, level or intensity.
#: {{ux|en|You need to tone '''down''' the rhetoric.}}
#: {{ux|en|Please turn the music '''down'''!}}
# So as to reduce size, weight or volume.
#: {{ux|en|Trim the stick '''down''' to a length of about twelve inches.}}
#: {{ux|en|Thanks to my strict diet, I've slimmed '''down''' to eleven stone.}}
#: {{ux|en|Boil the mixture '''down''' to a syrupy consistency.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1788|author=Mary Cole (cook)|title=The Lady's Complete Guide; or, Cookery in all its Branches|location=London|publisher=G. Kearsley|oclc=6545073|page=92|passage=ſtew it gently till quite tender, then take it up and boil '''down''' the gravy in the pan to a quart}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=29 Aug 81|volume=9|number=7|journal=Gay Community News|page=4|author=Nancy Wechsler|title=Pornography and the Lawyers Guild|text=At that point I perhaps should have gone back through the interview and changed what I said — slightly re-worded it to better reflect my feelings about the two resolutions. But I did not think to do that. I was caught up in the crunch of trying to get it all ready for publication, and edit it '''''down''''', not add more explanations to it.}}
# From less to greater detail.
#: {{ux|en|This spreadsheet lets you drill '''down''' to daily or even hourly sales figures.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847|magazine=w:The Economist
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems Boundary problems]
|passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too. GDP measures the total value of output in an economic territory. Its apparent simplicity explains why it is scrutinised '''down''' to tenths of a percentage point every month.}}
# From a remoter or higher antiquity.
#: {{ux|en|These traditions have been handed '''down''' over generations.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=June 17, 1825|author=w:Daniel Webster|title=An address delivered at the laying of the corner stone of the Bunker Hill monument|location=Boston|publisher=Cummings, Hilliard, and Co.|oclc=228718257|page=12|passage=Venerable men! you have come '''down''' to us from a former generation.}}
# Into a state of non-[[operation]].
#: {{ux|en|The computer has been shut '''down'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|They closed the shop '''down'''.}}
# So as to secure or compress something to the floor, ground, or other (usually horizontal) surface.
#: {{ux|en|We need to nail '''down''' this carpet so people don't keep tripping over it.}}
# On [[paper]] (or in a [[durable]] [[record]]).
#: {{ux|en|You need to write '''down''' what happened while it's still fresh in your mind.}}
# So as to be [[cow]]ed into [[silence]].
#: {{ux|en|The speaker was heckled and shouted '''down'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The comedy club's audience was known for hooting '''down''' timid performers.}}
# As a [[down payment]].
#: {{ux|en|We put £100 '''down''' on a new sofa.}}
#: {{ux|en|You can have it, no money '''down'''.}}
# {{lb|en|crosswords, in relation to a numbered clued word}} In a downwards direction; vertically.
#: {{ux|en|I'm stuck on 11 '''down'''.}}
# {{non-gloss|Used with verbs to indicate that the action of the verb was carried to some state of completion, permanence, or success rather than being of indefinite duration.}}
#: {{ux|en|He closed operations. / He closed '''down''' operations.}}
#: {{ux|en|He chased answers. / He chased '''down''' answers.}}
# {{lb|en|sentence substitute|imperative}} [[get down|Get down]].
#: {{ux|en|'''Down''', boy! {{qualifier|such as to direct a dog to stand on four legs from two, or to sit from standing on four legs.}}}}

=====Usage notes=====
* '''Down''' can be used with verbs in ways that change the meaning of the verb in ways not entirely predictable from the meanings of the '''down''' and the verb, though related to them. See [[:Category:English phrasal verbs formed with "down"]].

* {{antsense|into a state of non-operation}} {{l|en|up}}

* {{antsense|in crosswords}} {{l|en|across}}
* {{antsense|forward, straight ahead}} {{l|en|back}};  {{l|en|backwards}};  {{l|en|rearwards}}

====Preposition====
{{en-head|prep}}

# From the [[higher]] [[end]] to the [[lower]] of.
#: {{ux|en|The ball rolled '''down''' the hill.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=We expressed our readiness, and in ten minutes were in the station wagon, rolling rapidly '''down''' the long drive, for it was then after nine. We passed on the way the van of the guests from Asquith.}}
# From [[north]] to [[south]] of.
#: {{ux|en|We sailed '''down''' the eastern seaboard.}}
# Towards the mouth of (a river); in the direction of flow of.
#: {{ux|en|In this game we float sticks '''down''' the river.}}
# From one end to another of (in any direction); [[along]].
#: {{ux|en|The bus went '''down''' the street.}}
#: {{ux|en|They walked '''down''' the beach holding hands.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|work=Skip Boring|date=2026-08-07|author=Nicholas Muhoro|title=Korrina Malinoski, 26, Vanished After an Argument in 1987. Less Than a Year Later, Her 11-Year-Old Daughter Disappeared Too|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260807235024/https://skipboring.com/korrina-malinoski-annette-sagers-disappearance/|text=She got into her Dodge Omni and drove '''down''' the curving driveway towards the plantation’s main gate and onto Highway 52.}}

=====Usage notes=====
In many senses, using this adjective in an attributive position (before the noun) is avoided in everyday Standard English:
: {{ux|en|The system is '''down'''. / ''{{q|nonstandard}}'' They were fixing the '''down''' system.}}
Compare a synonym, {{m|en|faulty}}, which can be used either predicatively or attributively:
: {{ux|en|The system is '''faulty'''. / They were fixing the '''faulty''' system.}} (both acceptable)
In certain specialised uses (such as the veterinary medicine, timber and rail transport senses), there is no avoidance of the attributive placement, which is used freely.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[knock down|knock]] (someone or something) [[knock down|down]]; to cause to come down; to [[fell]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|The storm '''downed''' several old trees along the highway.}}
#: {{ux|en|A single rifle shot '''downed''' the mighty beast.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} Specifically, to cause (something in the air) to [[fall]] to the [[ground]]; to bring down (with a [[missile]] etc.). {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|The helicopter was '''downed''' by a surface-to-air missile.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[lower]]; to put (something) down. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|The bell rang for lunch, and the workers '''downed''' their tools.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To [[defeat]]; to [[overpower]]. {{defdate|from 17th. c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1725|author=Philip Sidney|title=The works of the Honourable Sir Philip Sidney, kt., in prose and verse|location=London|publisher=W. Innys|oclc=18146617|page=156|passage=To '''down''' proud hearts that would not willing die.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[disparage]]; to [[put down]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1779|author=w:Frances Burney|title=Journals & Letters|page=141|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2001
|passage=‘I remember how you '''downed''' Beauclerk and Hamilton, ''the Wits'', once at our House, – when they talked of ''Ghosts''.’}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=12 Apr 86|journal=Gay Community News|page=3|author=Anonymous|title=One Day I'll Write a Book on This|text=Now you have a social worker who '''downs''' women who are gay! {{...}} I have met a woman and fell in love with her and I still get humiliated and discriminated against because he (social worker) is against homosexuality and is causing a lot of confusion here.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|rare|or|obsolete}} To go or come down; to [[descend]]. {{defdate|from 17th. c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1933|quotee=Samuel Pepys ('''1664''', February 2nd)|author=Arthur Bryant|title=Samuel Pepys: The Man in the Making|location=New York|publisher=Macmillan|oclc=247768037|page=215|passage=...that is, that the trade of the world is too little for us two, therefore one must '''down'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[drink]] or [[swallow]], especially without stopping before the [[vessel]] containing the liquid is empty. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''downed''' an ale and ordered another.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2022 November 30|author=Paul Bigland|title=Destination Oban: a Sunday in Scotland|journal=RAIL|issue=971|page=75|text=After watching people '''downing''' drink on the train, I am in need of slaking my own thirst, so I pop into the station's ''Centurion Bar''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|American football|Canadian football}} To render (the [[ball]]) [[dead]], typically by [[touch]]ing the [[ground]] while in [[possession]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''downed''' it at the seven-yard line.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|golf|pocket billiards}} To [[sink]] (a [[ball]]) into a [[hole]] or [[pocket]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''downed''' two balls on the break.}}

{{en-noun}}

# A [[negative]] aspect; a [[downer]], a [[downside]].
#: {{ux|en|I love almost everything about my job. The only '''down''' is that I can't take Saturdays off.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} A [[grudge]] ({{m|en|on}} someone).
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1974|author=w:GB Edwards|title=The Book of Ebenezer Le Page|page=10|year_published=2007|location=New York
|passage=She had a '''down''' on me. I don't know what for, I'm sure; because I never said a word.}}
# A [[downer]], [[depressant]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=29 Dec 84|volume=12|number=25|journal=Gay Community News|page=4|author=Gena Spero|title=Innocent Lesbian In Prison|text=I am on drugs that I don't need to be on. They feel if I'm on a lot of '''downs''', then I won't complain about my prison life}}
# An act of swallowing an entire drink at once.
# {{lb|en|American football}} A single play, from the time the ball is snapped (the start) to the time the whistle is blown (the end) when the ball ''is down'', or ''is downed''.
#: {{ux|en|I bet after the third '''down''', the kicker will replace the quarterback on the field.}}
# {{lb|en|crosswords}} A clue whose solution runs [[vertical]]ly in the [[grid]].
#: {{ux|en|I haven't solved 12 or 13 across, but I've got most of the '''downs'''.}}
# {{lb|en|gambling}} The [[shift]] or period of time during which a [[dealer]] manages a given table before rotating<!-- being pushed --> to the next table at a [[casino]] or [[cardroom]], which is often 30 minutes.
# A downstairs room of a two-story house.
#: {{ux|en|She lives in a two-up two-'''down'''.}}
# [[down payment|Down payment]].
# The lightest [[quark]] with a charge number of &minus;{{frac|1|3}}.

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|id=hill|:inh|enm:doune<ety:inh<ang:dūn>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|doune}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dūn}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dūnā|*dūn|t=sandhill, dune}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain origin}}. Perhaps from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dūnaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*dūnǭ|t=pile, heap}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-|t=smoke, haze, dust}}. 

Alternatively, perhaps borrowed from {{der|en|cel-pro|*dūnom||hill; hillfort}} (compare {{cog|cy|din||city, fort, stronghold}}, {{cog|ga|dún||hill, fort}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-||to finish, come full circle}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|fy|dún||dune, sandhill}}, {{cog|nl|duin||dune, sandhill}}, {{cog|de|Düne||dune}}. More at {{m|en|town}}; akin to {{m|en|dune}}. {{doublet|en|Down}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|especially|southern England|also Australia|often plural|often in place names}} A [[hill]]; in England, especially a chalk hill.
#: {{ux|en|We went for a walk over the '''downs'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The North '''Downs''' are a ridge of chalk hills in south east England.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|4|1|text=And with each end of thy blue bow [[dost]] crown <br> My [[bosky]] acres and my unshrubb'd '''down'''}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1691|author=John Ray|title=The Wisdom of God Manifested in the Works of the Creation|location=London|publisher=Pr. for S. Smith|oclc=49840862|passage=...as they muſt needs acknowledge who have been on the '''Downs''' of Suſſex, and enjoyed that ravishing Proſpect of the Sea on one Hand, and the Country far and wide on the other.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1842|author=Alfred Tennyson|title=Poems|location=London|publisher=Edward Moxon|oclc=896031040|page=198|chapter=Lady Clare|passage=She went by dale, and she went by '''down''', <br> With a single rose in her hair.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1898
|author=[[w:Herbert George Wells|H. G. Wells]]
|title=Certain Personal Matters: A Collection of Material, Mainly Autobiographical
|url=https://archive.org/details/certainpersonal00wellgoog/
|publisher=w:Lawrence & Bullen
|OCLC=1120852385
|page=256
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/certainpersonal00wellgoog/page/n247/
|text=The amateur nature-lover proceeds over the '''down''', appreciating all this as hard as he can appreciate, and anon gazing up at the grey and white cloud shapes melting slowly from this form to that, and showing lakes, and wide expanses, and serene distances of blue between their gaps.}}
# {{lb|en|usually|in the plural}} A field, especially one used for horse racing.
# {{lb|en|UK|mostly|in the plural}} A tract of poor, sandy, undulating or hilly land near the sea, covered with fine turf which serves chiefly for the grazing of sheep.
#* {{quote-web|en|year=1636|author=George Sandys|title=A Paraphrase Vpon Iob|work=Early English Books|url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo/A11474.0001.001/1:12?rgn=div1;view=fulltext|passage=Seven thousand broad-taild Sheepe gras'd on his '''Downes''';}}

===Etymology 3===
{{etymon|en|id=feathers|:inh|enm:doun<id:feathers>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|doun}}, from {{der|en|non|dúnn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*dūnaz||down}}, which is related to {{m|gem-pro|*dauniz||(pleasant) smell}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*dʰowh₂-nis}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|Duune||fluff, down}}, {{cog|de|Daune||down}} and {{cog|da|dun||down}}.

====Noun====
[[File:Donsvlokje.jpg|thumb|Down feather ({{senseno|en|feathers}})]]
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|feathers}} Soft, [[fluffy]] immature [[feather]]s which grow on young birds. Used as insulating material in [[duvet]]s, [[sleeping bag]]s and [[jacket]]s.
# {{senseid|en|pubescence}} {{lb|en|botany}} The [[pubescence]] of [[plant]]s; the hairy crown or envelope of the seeds of certain plants, such as the [[thistle]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1718|author=Nicholas Culpeper|title=The English Physician Enlarged|location=London|publisher=W. Churchill|oclc=316759094|page=120|passage='''Down''' or Cotton-Thiſtle. This hath many large Leaves lying on the Ground, ſomewhat cut in, and as it were crumpled on the Edges, of a green Colour on the upper ſide, but covered with long hairy Wool or Cottony '''Down''', ſet with moſt ſharp and cruel pricks}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1998|author=Valerie Worth|title=The Crone's Book of Charms and Spells|location=Minnesota|publisher=Llewellyn Publications|isbn=1567188117|page=152|passage=No candle should light it, neither should any flower adorn it, save for several dried stalks of old and withered thistles, their heads pale with silken '''down''', held in a common glass jar.}}
# The soft hair of the face when beginning to appear.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1717|author=John Dryden|title=The Dramatick Works of John Dryden, Esq.|location=London|publisher=Jacob Tonson|volume=the fourth|oclc=83307675|page=136|passage=But love him as he was, when youthful Grace, <br> And the firſt '''Down''' began to ſhade his face}}
#* {{RQ:Turgenev Fathers and Sons|chapter=I|page=1|passage=The servant to whom he put this question was a young fellow with chubby cheeks, small, dull eyes, and a round chin, covered with a colorless '''down'''.}}
# That which is made of down, as a bed or pillow; that which affords ease and repose, like a bed of down.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:Thomas Southerne|Tho[mas] Southerne]]|title=Oroonoko: A Tragedy{{nb...|as It is Acted at the Theatre-Royal, by His Majesty’s Servants.}}|location=London|publisher={{...|Printed for}} [[w:Henry Playford|H[enry] Playford]]{{nb...|in the Temple-Change.}}; B[enjamin] Tooke{{nb...|at the Middle-Temple-Gate.}}; [a]nd S. Buckley{{nb...|at the Dolphin against St. Dunstan’s Church in Fleetstreet.}}|year=1696|section=act V, scene the last [iv]|pages=76–77|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/oroonokotragedya00sout/page/76/mode/1up|oclc=1227540146|passage=Thou boſom Softneſs! '''Down''' of all my Cares! <br> I cou'd recline my thoughts upon this Breaſt <br> To a forgetfulneſs of all my Griefs, <br> And yet be happy: but it wonnot be.}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|passage=When in the '''down''' I sink my head, <br> Sleep, Death's twin brother, times my breath.}}
